title: Hapgood's earth crustal displacement

tellings.quote: to Hapkut. It's that the North Pole was where Hudson Bay is today

plain: The North Pole was once where Hudson Bay in Canada is today, because the Earth's outer crust slid as a whole across the planet and moved the poles. This is the idea of a writer named Charles Hapgood, known as earth crustal displacement, and the researcher Jason Jorjani sums it up for Michels without naming a further source. If true, lands such as Antarctica would once have sat in a warmer place, which would change how we read the deep past.
